# 2 Samuel Chapter 7 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 174r–175v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2SA_007_page_001.jpg, 2SA_007_page_002.jpg, 2SA_007_page_003.jpg

---

**1** Once the king was settled in his palace and the LORD had given him peace on every side from all his enemies, **2** David said to Nathan the prophet, "Look — I live in a house of cedar, while the ark of God sits inside tent curtains."

**3** Nathan told the king, "Whatever you have in mind, go ahead — the LORD is with you."

**4** But that night, the word of the LORD came to Nathan: **5** "Go tell my servant David: This is what the LORD says — Are you the one to build me a house to live in? **6** I have never lived in a house from the day I brought Israel up out of Egypt until today. I have been on the move — in a tent, in a tabernacle. **7** Wherever I traveled with the Israelites, did I ever say to any of the leaders I appointed to shepherd my people Israel, 'Why haven't you built me a house of cedar?'

**8** "So tell my servant David: This is what the LORD of Hosts says — I took you from the pasture, from herding sheep, to be ruler over my people Israel. **9** I have been with you everywhere you went. I have destroyed all your enemies before you. And I will make your name as great as any of the greatest names on earth. **10** I will provide a place for my people Israel and plant them there, so they can live in a home of their own and never be disturbed again. Violent people will no longer oppress them as they did before, **11** ever since the time I appointed judges over my people Israel. I will give you rest from all your enemies.

"And the LORD declares this to you: the LORD himself will build you a house.

**12** "When your life is over and you rest with your ancestors, I will raise up your offspring after you — one who comes from your own body — and I will establish his kingdom. **13** He is the one who will build a house for my name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever. **14** I will be a father to him, and he will be a son to me. When he does wrong, I will discipline him with a human rod and with human blows. **15** But my faithful love will never leave him, the way I withdrew it from Saul when I removed him to make way for you. **16** Your house and your kingdom will endure forever before you. Your throne will be established forever."

**17** Nathan reported all of this to David — every word, every vision.

**18** King David went in and sat before the LORD. "Who am I, Lord GOD," he said, "and what is my family, that you have brought me this far? **19** And as if that were not enough, Lord GOD, you have also spoken about the future of your servant's family for generations to come. Is this your plan for all humanity, Lord GOD?

**20** What more can David say to you? You know your servant, Lord GOD. **21** For the sake of your promise and out of your own heart, you have done all this — and made it known to your servant.

**22** How great you are, LORD God! There is no one like you. There is no God but you — everything we have ever heard confirms it.

**23** And who is like your people Israel? — the one nation on earth that God went out to redeem as his own, to make a name for himself, to do great and terrifying things for your land, driving out nations and their gods before the people you rescued from Egypt.

**24** You made Israel your own people forever, and you, LORD, became their God.

**25** Now, LORD God, keep forever the promise you made about your servant and his house. Do what you have said. **26** Let your name be honored forever: 'The LORD of Hosts is God over Israel!' And let the house of your servant David stand firm before you.

**27** For you, LORD of Hosts, God of Israel, have opened your servant's ears with this revelation: 'I will build you a house.' That is why your servant has dared to pray this prayer to you.

**28** Lord GOD, you are God! Your words are truth, and you have promised this good thing to your servant. **29** Now be pleased to bless the house of your servant, that it may continue forever in your presence. For you, Lord GOD, have spoken — and by your blessing let your servant's house be blessed forever."

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**Verse 5 — "Are you the one?":** The Hebrew puts enormous emphasis on the pronoun: *ha-attah* — "YOU — will you build me a house?" The question is not a rejection of a temple but a dramatic reversal: God does not need David to build him a house. God will build David a house. The irony is breathtaking.

**Verse 6 — "on the move":** The Hebrew *mithalekh* is a hitpael participle — "walking about," "moving about." God presents himself as a nomad-deity, deliberately un-housed, traveling with his people. This is a theological statement: YHWH is not a static, localized god like the gods of the nations. He goes where his people go.

**Verse 11 — The great reversal:** This is the pivot-point of the chapter and one of the most important verses in the Hebrew Bible. David wanted to build God a *bayit* (house/temple). God responds: I will build you a *bayit* (house/dynasty). The entire Davidic covenant theology hangs on this wordplay. The temple will be built — but by David's son, not David. And the truly lasting thing that God builds is not stone but lineage.

**Verse 14 — "a human rod":** The phrase *shevet anashim* (rod of men) and *nig'ey bney adam* (blows of human beings) mean that God will use human agents and human consequences to discipline David's offspring — not catastrophic divine destruction. The promise is that the covenant will survive even the worst failures of David's descendants.

**Verse 15 — "my faithful love will never leave him":** Hebrew *chasdi* — my *hesed*, my covenant-faithfulness. This is the unconditional core of the Davidic covenant. God removed his *hesed* from Saul; he will never remove it from David's line. The contrast is explicit and absolute.

**Verse 19 — "Is this your plan for all humanity?":** The Hebrew *torat ha-adam* is one of the most mysterious phrases in the Bible. Literally "the instruction/law of the human" or "the charter of mankind." David seems to be asking: is this covenant just about my family, or are you revealing something about humanity's ultimate destiny? The phrase has been read as eschatological, messianic, and universal — it is all of these.

*— PNEUMA*
